files.purpose: The MCP page of the Settings window. Top to bottom it shows a lead card ("Connected servers lead"), a "Connected" card with one row per connected catalog server (switch plus an ellipsis menu for Refresh / Show tools / Disconnect), a "Custom" section listing the user's own servers with an "Add server" row, then one two-column grid per MCPCategory of catalog server cards with Connect / Sign in / Fix it / Try again actions, and a closing footnote. Every list follows the settings search query. When a server becomes connected it stays in the grid for 900 ms showing a checkmark pop and plays SettleChime, then moves into Connected. The file also holds the custom-server add/edit popover: variable names go into the server record, plain values into mcp.json and locked values into the Keychain. It also holds the hover info popover (connection, needs, tool chips, docs link), a wrapping FlowLayout, and the shared MCPIcon view used by other MCP views.

side_effects: On model.mcp.states change (skipped entirely when reduceMotion): `for (id, state) in current where state.isConnected && !(previous[id]?.isConnected ?? false) { celebrating.insert(id); SettleChime.play(); Task { @MainActor in try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(900)); celebrating.remove(id) } }` (lines 64-74). model.mcp.states is MCPStore's single `[String: MCPConnectionState]` dictionary, which also holds custom server ids (MCPStore.swift:185 `states[server.id] = .notConnected`; MCPCustom.swift:100 the custom catalogEntry uses `id: id`), so connecting a CUSTOM server also plays SettleChime although customs never appear in the grid or the Connected card. The chime plays once per newly connected id, so several ids connecting in one update play several chimes. The handler is `.onChange` on the MCPSettingsPage view, so the chime and the celebration happen only while the MCP settings page is on screen.
Connect / Sign in / Try again: entry.needsInput false -> model.mcp.connect(entry); true -> MCPKeyPanel.shared.present(entry:model:).

MCPServerCard.onChange(of: state) (lines 284-290): `if case .needsSetup(let guide) = now { MCPSetupPanel.shared.present(entry: entry, guide: guide, model: model) }`, which also opens the guide page in the browser. The observer lives on the card, and a card exists only for a grid entry that is not connected (or is celebrating) and matches the search, while the Settings MCP page is shown. With the page closed or the card filtered out, no panel opens by itself. The port must keep this on the card, not in a global state observer.

Row menus call model.mcp.refresh / disconnect / deleteCustom; the switch calls model.mcp.setEnabled(_:for:). None of these asks for confirmation: `PopoverItem("Delete", symbol: "trash", isDestructive: true) { model.mcp.deleteCustom(server) }` (lines 564-566) and both "Disconnect" items (lines 190-192, 560-562) pass no `confirmation:` and act at once. Every PopoverItem closes its own popover before running the action (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Popovers.swift:271-273: `if let close = closePopoverBox?.close { close() } else { dismiss() }` then `Task { @MainActor in action() }`), so Refresh, Disconnect and Delete close the menu too; "Show tools" (line 186) and "Edit" (line 557) additionally set `showMenu = false` themselves before raising their second popover.

Editor save writes the server via saveCustom and the values via saveCustomValues (plain -> mcp.json, locked -> Keychain, per comments); then `if wasConnected, let entry = model.mcp.entry(for: draft.id) { model.mcp.refresh(entry) }` with `let wasConnected = server.map { model.mcp.state(for: $0.id).isConnected } ?? false` (line 866): only an edit of an existing server (server != nil) can refresh; the adding editor (server nil, including a second save through savedID after a Keychain failure) never refreshes; then dismiss().
Editor onAppear when editing reads stored values through model.mcp.storedValue(server:field:secret:) (Keychain for secret ones).

Link("Read the docs") opens entry.docsURL in the default browser; it is rendered only `if let url = URL(string: entry.docsURL)` (line 1010), so an entry whose docsURL does not parse (custom entries set `docsURL: ""`, MCPCustom.swift:112) shows no link.

PORT WARNING: .whitespaces does not include newline characters, so on Windows a multi-line text box that yields "\r\n" would leave a trailing "\r" in every argument and keep a "\r"-only line; the port must split on CRLF (or strip "\r") to reach parity; url = url.trimmed; env (stdio) or headers (http) = [Variable(key: key trimmed of .whitespaces, isSecret)] with empty keys dropped. feature_notes: Search matching covers name, vendor, summary, id and sampleTools (case-insensitive, localized). The Custom section uses the same matcher on server.catalogEntry(). The Connected card is NOT filtered by the query.

A connected catalog server is removed from the grid and shown in Connected, except while celebrating: for 900 ms it stays in the grid showing the success view and is excluded from Connected (`!celebrating.contains($0.id)`, line 21). In the grid it is kept only if it also matches the search (`(!model.mcp.state(for: entry.id).isConnected || celebrating.contains(entry.id)) && Self.matches(entry, query: query)`, lines 28-29), so a server that connects while a search hides it appears in neither list for those 900 ms. Under reduce motion there is no celebration and no chime: it moves at once.
Connected rows are sorted by name with plain String `<` (not localized).
The needsSetup state opens MCPSetupPanel automatically from the card's onChange(of: state), and the "Fix it" button reopens it. The Custom row has the "Fix it" button but no automatic onChange.

MCPHoverInfoButton timing: reconsider() cancels the pending task; wanted = isOverButton || isOverPopover; if wanted differs from isPresented, it waits 220 ms (open) or 320 ms (close) and applies only if the hover state still matches and the task was not cancelled. Clicking toggles immediately and cancels the pending task.

Info popover "Connects" text: stdio -> "Runs on this Mac through \(command) (\(package))." where package is the first arg not starting with "-" (else command); http -> "Remote server at \(host)."; oauth -> "Remote server at \(host of entry.fill(url, values: [:])). You sign in once in your browser." Host is URL(string:)?.host() or the raw string.

Info popover "Needs" text: no fields -> "Only your sign-in." (OAuth) or "Nothing — press Connect."; otherwise the required labels, then "optional: " + optional labels joined ", " and lowercased, all joined "; " with a trailing ".".
The "Change the <label>…" button appears for the first non-required field only.

Editor: the name gets focus only when adding. When editing, onAppear fills each variable's value from model.mcp.storedValue(server: id, field: key, secret: isSecret). Rows are identified by UUID, so editing a key does not rebuild the row. The variable list survives a kind switch (it is written to env for stdio and headers for http).

Editor save(): builds draft; wasConnected = `server.map { model.mcp.state(for: $0.id).isConnected } ?? false` (always false when adding); if saveCustom(draft, replacing: server?.id ?? savedID) returns a failure, error = failure.message and stop. Then savedID = draft.id. If saveCustomValues(keptValues, for: draft.id, replacingFieldsOf: server?.catalogEntry()) returns false, error = "The Keychain could not save a value. Keep this editor open and try again." and stop. If it was connected and model.mcp.entry(for: draft.id) exists, refresh it. Then dismiss().
Editor height: 450 base for stdio, 320 for http, plus 34 per variable row, capped at 560; the form scrolls inside, and the error text and Save button stay pinned below the scroll view.

FlowLayout wraps a subview to a new row when x > 0 (or > minX) and x + width exceeds the proposed width / bounds.maxX; the row gap equals the spacing (6); the reported width is proposal.width, or the widest row when there is none.
MCPConnectedRow's switch getter defaults to true when connection is nil; the tool count prefers the .connected(count) payload and falls back to connection?.tools.count.

(1) Font sizes became text styles everywhere they were fixed: size 22 -> .title (lead icon); 13 -> .body (row/card names, lead title, ellipsis icons, add-row icon and label); 12 -> .callout (lead body, facts, card summary, success label, custom empty text, lock/minus/add-label icons, info button icon, info summary, change-field button, docs link); 11 -> .subheadline (tool counts, vendor, failure/needsSetup text, Connecting/Waiting, tools popover name and summary, custom status lines, editor subtitle, field labels, info subtitle, Tools/detail labels, footnote); 9 bold -> .caption2 bold (docs arrow). Fixed sizes 14 (editor/info titles), 11.5 (detail value), 10.5 (sample tools, chips, editor captions) and 34 (success checkmark `.font(.system(size: 34))`, line 363; also MCPSetupPanel.swift:242) are unchanged. (2) query/command/url trimming changed from trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) to the `.trimmed` extension, which is `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }` (DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:132): the same character set, so no behaviour change; the port keeps the whitespace-and-newline trim. (3) MCPCustomEditor: new constants width 380, sectionSpacing 12 (was 14), outerPadding 16 (was 18), variableRowHeight 34; the fixed 380x560 frame became width 380 with the computed height (450 stdio / 320 http + 34 per row, max 560); error and Save moved into a `footer` (VStack spacing 10, Spacer(minLength: 0)); the close xmark gained a 24x24 frame, contentShape and accessibilityLabel "Close"; the Name field gained `.textFieldStyle(.plain)` and `.focusEffectDisabled()` (no focus ring; the B1 field had neither) and became .title3 semibold primaryText with padding 10/7 and the field surface (was a default TextField at `.font(.system(size: 12))`); editorField, secureEditorField and the Arguments TextEditor changed from `.font(.system(size: 12, design: .monospaced))` to `.font(.system(.callout, design: .monospaced))`; the footer error text changed from `.font(.system(size: 11))` to `.font(.system(.subheadline))` (lines 691-696); editor fields went from padding h 8 with radius-8 overlay(0.06) to padding h 10 with the new mcpFieldSurface (radius 9); the Arguments TextEditor padding went from 4/3 to 6/4. (4) Added `private extension View { func mcpFieldSurface() }`.
unresolved_questions: Point sizes for the SwiftUI text styles on macOS (.title, .title3, .body, .callout, .subheadline, .caption2 here; .footnote in MCPSetupPanel) are not stated in either B2 file. The B1 fixed sizes they replaced (22, 13, 12, 11, 9) are what B1 rendered, but B2 states no numbers, so a mapping such as .caption2 = 9 pt is NOT supported by the source and must come from the port contract or a measurement.
MCPCatalog contents, MCPCategory titles and order, SettleChime sound, and the mcp.json / Keychain behaviour of saveCustom and saveCustomValues live in other files.
Chrome.sectionSpacing, Chrome.rowControlTrailingPadding and the Chrome colour values are defined elsewhere.

files.purpose: A floating, non-activating AppKit NSPanel singleton (MCPSetupPanel.shared). It appears when an MCP server refuses a connection because of something on the server's side (MCPConnectionState.needsSetup(guide)). As it appears it opens the guide's web page in the default browser and sits in the top-right corner of the main screen showing the reason, numbered steps, a page button and "Check again". After a re-check it shows a warning or error line. When the server connects it shows a success view and closes itself after 1.2 s. The panel resizes to its SwiftUI content while keeping its top edge fixed, can be dragged by its background, and closes on Escape (keyCode 53) or its own xmark.

side_effects: present() opens guide.pageURL in the default browser, only `if let url = URL(string: guide.pageURL) { NSWorkspace.shared.open(url) }` (lines 28-30), each time it builds the panel for a new presentation (not when it is already presenting the same entry, which only orders the panel front).
The "page label" button opens guide.pageURL again, under the same `if let url = URL(string: guide.pageURL)` guard (lines 133-137); "Check again" calls model.mcp.refresh(entry).

Installs an app-wide local keyDown monitor while shown (`NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown)`, lines 88-95); Escape (keyCode 53) closes the panel and swallows the event (`return nil`) only while the panel is visible. The guard checks only `self.panel?.isVisible == true, event.keyCode == 53`, not which window has focus, so while the app is active an Escape meant for another Droppy window (for example a Settings text field) is swallowed and closes the panel. A local monitor receives only key events delivered to this app, and the panel is `.nonactivatingPanel` shown with orderFrontRegardless(), so Escape has no effect while another app (such as the browser present() may just have opened) is frontmost.

On connect, closes the panel 1.2 s later through onDone (MCPSetupPanel.close): `Task { @MainActor in try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.2)); onDone() }` (lines 186-192) is unstructured and never cancelled, and onDone is `{ [weak self] in self?.close() }` (line 31), which orders out the one shared panel. If another entry is presented into the panel within those 1.2 s, the old task still closes it.

Positioning in Cocoa bottom-left screen coordinates: origin x = visibleFrame.maxX - 400 - 24, y = visibleFrame.maxY - frame.height - 24 (top-right, 24 pt inset); fit() grows or shrinks downward by adjusting origin.y. On Windows (top-left origin) this is top = workArea.top + 24.

files.purpose: The Models page of Settings, where the user picks which models the composer's model picker offers. The top "Your models" card lists the chosen models (ModelPin) in picker order. They can be reordered by dragging a grip with live neighbour swaps and haptics, and removed with a minus button. Clicking a row opens an EffortSliderCard popover that sets that model's default reasoning effort and fast mode for new chats. Below, each available provider has a collapsible section listing its model catalogue with add/remove buttons, capped at AppSettings.modelListLimit. A collapsed section shows only the chosen models, and the collapse state lives on the page so the search does not reset it. Everything is filtered by the settings search query, and filtering does not animate.

feature_notes: Reorder: on the first drag change for a pin, drag = RowDrag(id: pin) and closedHand is pushed. The translation is set without animation. The order is re-read from visiblePins(query.trimmed) on every move. drag.settle(order:heights: rowHeights, fallbackHeight: 54) calls moveModel inside withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.82)), and a move triggers the .alignment haptic. dragEnded pops the cursor and resets drag with .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8). While searching, swaps happen against visible neighbours, so hidden pins keep their place relative to them.

Grip cursor handling: on hover it pushes openHand, and on leave it pops, but only when not dragging. onDisappear pops if still hovering. When isDragged turns false and the pointer is off the grip, it pops the leftover open hand.
rowHeights is pruned to the current pins whenever its count exceeds pins.count.
The "Your models" rows use a non-lazy VStack on purpose: a lazy stack animated reordered rows from the origin and ignored zIndex.

Row summary: provider.displayName, then (when the model has efforts) ModelOption.effortTitle(preference.effort ?? option.defaultEffort ?? "") + " effort", then "Fast" when preference.fastMode and option.supportsFast; joined " · ".
Removing from the Your models row animates with Chrome.panelSlide. A catalogue toggle animates with Chrome.panelSlide only when not filtering; mid-search it applies instantly.

Provider section visibility: while filtering, only matching models; otherwise all models when expanded, or only models in the list when collapsed. The first visible row has no divider. The card is visible when expanded, filtering, or any row is visible, so collapsed with nothing chosen hides the card. Hidden rows and a hidden card are disabled, not hit-testable, and hidden from accessibility. The rows always walk the full catalogue in catalogue order, and each row opens or closes through ChromeRevealLayout with clipping.
Search: the page trims the query (query.trimmed); matches() does not trim again. Providers are listed in registry.availableProviders order.

The list is full when settings.modelList.count >= AppSettings.modelListLimit (`static let modelListLimit = 15`, DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:182; addToModelList also guards `modelList.count < Self.modelListLimit`, AppSettings.swift:828), so the help text reads "The picker holds up to 15 models"; then only already-added models can be toggled (removed).

B1->B2: 170 changed lines (374 -> 452 lines). Added the page state `providerExpansion: [ProviderKind: Bool]` and passed ProviderModelsSection an `isExpanded` Binding (default true). Provider sections are now collapsible: the header became a ChromeQuietButtonStyle button with a chevron.right rotating to 90° and the help/accessibility strings "Hide the model list", "Show the model list", "Expanded", "Collapsed", "Shows or hides the model list". A collapsed section shows only chosen models, and collapsed with none chosen closes the card. ChromeCard was replaced by an eager VStack with Chrome.overlay(0.03) fill, Chrome.cardCornerRadius and a clip. Before, rows were a filtered `options` list with `index > 0` dividers; now they walk the full catalogue with separate ChromeRevealLayout reveals for divider and row, plus disabled / allowsHitTesting / accessibilityHidden on hidden rows. The empty-catalogue row is now wrapped in a reveal and checks catalogue.isEmpty (before: the filtered options.isEmpty). Toggling a model mid-search no longer animates. `.animation(nil, value: query)` was added. `query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` became `query.trimmed` in body and dragChanged; `.trimmed` is `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` (Text.swift:132), so no behaviour change. The provider pre-filter `registry.availableProviders.filter { provider in trimmed.isEmpty || registry.models(for: provider).contains { Self.matches(...) } }` (lines 25-27) is unchanged from B1 (B1 lines 22-23), and B1's `options` used the same matcher on the same trimmed query, so neither B1 nor B2 can show "No models loaded" mid-search; this is not a B2 behaviour change. The Your-models card, PinnedModelRow and RowControl are unchanged.
